title: Tenali Raman and the Gossip-Hunting Mynah

full_text:
Two arrogant and envious courtiers, Lord Malhar and Lord Vasudev, frequently gathered in the palace garden pavilions to whisper malicious gossip, mocking King Krishnadevaraya’s poetry and scheming against his ministers.
Knowing that walls have ears, they conducted their treasonous whispers inside a secluded arbor covered in thick passionflower vines.

Tenali Raman discovered their secret meeting spot.
Instead of denouncing them directly without proof, Tenali acquired a brilliant hill mynah bird—a creature renowned for its uncanny ability to mimic human voices with flawless accuracy.

For two weeks, Tenali secretly placed the mynah’s wicker cage hidden within the dense passionflower foliage above the courtiers' stone bench.
Whenever Malhar and Vasudev sat below, sipping wine and mocking the King, the clever bird listened quietly, absorbing their exact words, vocal tones, and chuckles.

During the grand royal festival of Vasantotsava, King Krishnadevaraya held court in the open garden pavilion before hundreds of dignitaries.
Tenali Raman entered carrying the mynah in an ornate golden cage covered with a silk veil.
'Maharaj,' announced Tenali, 'I have brought a remarkable royal songbird from the Nilgiris that can recite the most candid, unrehearsed poetry composed in your palace gardens!'

The King smiled: 'Let us hear its song, Tenali!'

Tenali pulled away the silk veil.
The mynah cocked its head, looked directly at Lord Malhar and Lord Vasudev sitting in the front row, and began reciting in Lord Malhar’s unmistakable, pompous nasal voice:
*‘The King thinks he is a poet, but his verses sound like an ox groaning in a ditch! He-he-he!’*

The court froze in stunned silence! Lord Malhar turned white as linen!
Then the mynah switched seamlessly to Lord Vasudev’s shrill, squeaky voice:
*‘Aye, Malhar! And when the treasury sends gold to the army, we shall pocket our twenty percent as usual before the fool notices!’*

The entire assembly gasped in horror!
Lord Vasudev collapsed onto the carpet in terror, while Lord Malhar began babbling incoherent apologies.
The King’s eyes blazed with righteous anger:
'Guards! Arrest these traitors! Audit their accounts immediately!'

The imperial audit revealed massive embezzlement by both courtiers. Their estates were confiscated, and they were sentenced to hard labor on the frontier fortresses.
King Krishnadevaraya embraced Tenali:
'Tenali, thy talking bird has unmasked treason that fifty spies could not detect!'
The clever mynah was appointed the official mascot of the imperial gardens, fed on sweet figs and almonds for the rest of its days.
moral: Those who whisper malicious slander behind closed doors are caught by the innocent mirrors of nature.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Tenali and the Talking Mynah"?
options: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By running away from every problem
